title: Momentum Module 7 Lesson 1: Momentum With Kinematics Dynamics custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt:
A particle $A$ of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest from a height of $1.8\text{ m}$ above the floor. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)
Find the speed with which $A$ hits the floor, and determine the impulse exerted on $A$ if it is brought to rest by the floor without rebounding.

Particle $A$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ moving at $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ collides directly with stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ on a rough horizontal surface and coalesces to form $C$. The coefficient of friction between $C$ and the surface is $\mu = 0.15$. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)
Find the common speed of $C$ immediately after collision, and calculate its deceleration due to friction.

A coalesced particle $C$ of mass $1.0\text{ kg}$ emerges from a collision with speed $2.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and slides along a rough horizontal floor with deceleration $1.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until it comes to rest. Calculate the distance travelled by $C$ before coming to rest.

A particle $A$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at the top of a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The length of the plane is $3.6\text{ m}$. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)
Find the speed of $A$ when it reaches the bottom of the plane.

A particle $A$ of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ is projected vertically upwards with speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$. At the highest point of its trajectory, $A$ collides with a particle $B$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ falling vertically downwards with speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)
Find the common speed of the particles immediately after impact if they coalesce.

A particle of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is struck by an impulse of magnitude $3.0\text{ N s}$, giving it an initial velocity along a rough horizontal plane. The frictional force opposing its motion is $2.0\text{ N}$. Calculate the time taken for the particle to come to rest.

questions.prompt: A particle $A$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest from a height of $3.2\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. Immediately upon reaching the ground, particle $A$ collides with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$. The two particles coalesce to form a combined particle $C$. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $A$ immediately before the collision, and the speed of $C$ immediately after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the loss in kinetic energy caused by the collision.

questions.prompt: A particle $A$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is moving with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ on a rough horizontal floor. It collides directly with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ on the floor. On impact, $A$ and $B$ coalesce to form a combined particle $C$. The coefficient of friction between $C$ and the floor is $\mu = 0.25$. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $C$ immediately after the collision, and find the frictional force acting on $C$ as it slides.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the distance that $C$ travels after the collision before coming to rest.

questions.prompt: A block $A$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is accelerated from rest along a smooth horizontal track by a constant horizontal driving force of $2.5\text{ N}$ for a distance of $4.0\text{ m}$. Block $A$ then enters a rough section of the track and collides directly with a stationary block $B$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$. On impact, $A$ and $B$ coalesce to form a combined body $C$. The coefficient of friction between $C$ and the rough track is $\mu = 0.32$. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $A$ immediately before the collision, and the speed of $C$ immediately after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the distance that $C$ travels along the rough track before coming to rest.

questions.prompt: A smooth slope of length $4.5\text{ m}$ is inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = 0.4$. A particle $A$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at the top of the slope. At the bottom of the slope, $A$ moves smoothly onto a smooth horizontal surface and collides directly with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$. In the collision, particle $A$ continues to move in the same direction with speed $1.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $A$ when it reaches the bottom of the slope.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $B$ immediately after the collision, and calculate the magnitude of the impulse exerted by $A$ on $B$.

questions.prompt: A particle $A$ of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ is projected vertically upwards with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from ground level. At the same instant, a particle $B$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest from a height of $20\text{ m}$ directly above $A$. The particles collide in mid-air. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the collision occurs $1.0\text{ s}$ after projection, and find the velocity of each particle immediately before they collide.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If $A$ and $B$ coalesce on impact, find the common velocity of the combined particle immediately after the collision, and determine the greatest height above the ground reached by the combined particle.

questions.prompt: A block $A$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is pulled up a rough plane inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\alpha = 0.6$ and $\cos\alpha = 0.8$, by a constant force of magnitude $6.0\text{ N}$ acting parallel to a line of greatest slope. The coefficient of friction between $A$ and the plane is $\mu_1 = 0.25$. Block $A$ starts from rest and travels a distance of $2.5\text{ m}$ to the top of the incline. At the top of the incline, the pulling force is removed and block $A$ moves smoothly onto a rough horizontal plane, where it collides directly with a stationary block $B$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$. On impact, $A$ and $B$ coalesce to form a single combined body $C$. The coefficient of friction between $C$ and the horizontal plane is $\mu_2 = 0.2$. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the acceleration of $A$ up the inclined plane is $4.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and find the speed of $A$ when it reaches the top of the incline.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $C$ immediately after the collision.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the total distance that $C$ slides along the horizontal plane before coming to rest.

questions.prompt: Two particles $P$ and $Q$, of masses $0.4\text{ kg}$ and $0.6\text{ kg}$ respectively, are connected by a light inextensible string of length $1.2\text{ m}$. Initially, particle $Q$ is held at rest on a horizontal table and particle $P$ is released from rest at the same level as $Q$ and falls vertically. The string becomes taut when $P$ has fallen $1.2\text{ m}$. Immediately after the string becomes taut, $Q$ is pulled off the table and both particles move vertically downwards together. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $P$ immediately before the string becomes taut, and show that the common speed of $P$ and $Q$ immediately after the string becomes taut is $1.96\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (or $\frac{2}{5}\sqrt{24}\text{ m s}^{-1} = \frac{4\sqrt{6}}{5}\text{ m s}^{-1}$).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the magnitude of the impulsive tension exerted by the string on $Q$ when the string becomes taut, and calculate the loss of mechanical energy caused by the jerk.
